newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP DRAGS AUSTRALIAN STOCKS DOWN TO NOON.
newsitem.headline: BHP DRAGS AUSTRALIAN STOCKS DOWN TO NOON.

text.p: *Stocks dip into red by midsession as bruised bellwether BHP drags market down. Volume 156.87 million, A$395.75 million value, 928 stocks traded, 301 steady, 321 up, 306 down.
A bruised BHP dragged the Australian share market below square by the midsession on Thursday as traders sold the bellwether down amid concerns over costs and the direction of its minerals division.

By 12.25 p.m. (0225 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 4.9 points lower at 2,722.2, while September share price index futures were three points lower at 2,741, an 18.8 point premium to the underlying index.
BHP's 42 cent or 2.3 percent fall to A$17.57 accounted for the nearly five point loss in the broader market, which was generally slightly firmer.

On Monday BHP announced the surprise departure of mineral division head Dick Carter. The company also flagged a cost blow-out at its hot briquetted iron (HBI) project in the Pilbara in Western Australia. "There is all sorts of guesswork about what is going to happen there," said a Sydney broker.
July labour force data failed to excite, with the numbers failing to spark fresh hopes of further interest rate cuts.
"I think they were pretty much in line. Maybe the market was looking for something in them but they didn't get (a lead) either way," said Morgan Stockbroking dealer John O'Neill.
On the upside, global miner Rio Tinto built on a strong London performance, adding 20 cents to A$21.00.

Elsewhere, Brambles Industries jumped to a record high of A$28.80 following the overnight release of results from GKN Plc, its partner in the Chep pallet business in the U.S. By noon Brambles shares had eased from their highs to be up 65 cents at A$28.63.

Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer Ltd was steady at A$6.90 after reporting a 5.8 percent increase in year sales to A$19.23 billion. The retailer said it maintained its view of second half profit growth similar to the first half.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields crept above their early lows after the July labour force report contained a surprise 52,500 jump in full-time employment. By 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), 10-year T-bonds were yielding 6.52 percent, down from Wednesday's 6.53 percent close.

The Australian dollar bounced 1/4 cent after jobs data failed to meet bearish expectations, so triggering a burst of short covering. By 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), the local dollar had pawed its way to US$0.7363/68 from an early US$0.7340/45.
